name: Pashhur
overview: Pashhur was a male Levite priest, identified as the son of Malchijah. He is noted in the biblical record as a priest involved in the post-exilic community, specifically mentioned among those who sealed the covenant document in Nehemiah 10:3. His priestly role and tribal affiliation highlight his service in the spiritual leadership of Israel during the restoration period.
namesAndTitles: The name Pashhur is a proper name that possibly means 'be quiet and round about,' reflecting a Hebrew etymology. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may suggest a character or role associated with calmness or encircling presence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Pashhur as the son of Malchijah and infers Jeroham as his father. He is also linked as a descendant of several Levite ancestors including Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Netanel, Jozabad, and Elasah, indicating a well-established priestly lineage. Additionally, Nehemiah 11:12 suggests Zechariah as a father figure, further situating him within a recognized priestly family.
scriptureSignificance: Pashhur's significance lies in his role as a priest during the critical period of Israel's return from exile and restoration of worship. His inclusion on the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10:3 underscores his commitment to the reestablishment of the covenant community under God's law. Through his priestly service, he contributed to the spiritual renewal and continuity of the Levitical priesthood in Jerusalem.
